plain.li: [write] Now, how to begin a letter to {NAME}.
[write] Let me get this down while it's clear in my head.
[write] A letter to {TOWN}, and in my best hand.
[write] I'll keep it short and say it plainly.
[write,theirLowtech] They'll read this out at their fire, so it had better be good.
[write,theirHightech] Short and to the point, they're busy people over there.
[written] There, that says what it needs to.
[written] Signed and folded, now someone just has to carry it.
[written] Done, and I didn't blot it once.
[hand] This is for {NAME}, and nobody else.
[hand] Carry it carefully, it matters to us.
[hand] Safe roads to you, and give them our best.
[hand,theirLowtech] Tell {NAME} it comes with the whole colony's regards.
[guest] So this is the colony I've heard about.
[guest] Thank you for asking me, it was a long road.
[guest,theirLowtech] I've walked three days to sit at your fire.
[call] Hello, this is the colony calling for {NAME}.
[call] Is this the line to {TOWN}?
[call] Static again, give it a moment.
[answer] Yes, we're here, go ahead.
[answer] Colony speaking, who's this?
[answer] Ah, {NAME}, thank you for calling back.
[talk] Yes, I understand.
[talk] That's good to hear.
[talk] Could you say that again, the line's poor.
[talk] We'd be glad to, of course.
[talk] I'll tell the others, they'll want to know.
[endwarm] Well, that went better than I'd hoped.
[endwarm] They were glad we called, I could hear it.
[endcordial] A good talk, short but good.
[endcordial] Friendly enough, I'd say.
[endcool] Polite, but they kept it brief.
[endcool] Hard to read them over the static.
[endcurt] Short with me, that one.
[endcurt] I don't think we were welcome on that line.
[endrefusal] Well, that was a no.
[endrefusal] They turned us down flat.
[endaide] An aide took a message, they'll call back.
[endaide] Not there right now, we'll hear back later.
[enddead] And the line's dead, wonderful.
[enddead] Lost them, nothing but hiss.
[endsilence] They listened, and then just cut the line.
[endsilence] Nothing back, not a word.

warm.li: [write] I hope this finds them well, truly.
[hand] Look after yourself on the way back.
[endwarm] I like them, I really do.

blunt.li: [write] No flowery words, just what needs saying.

cheerful.li: [endwarm] What lovely people they are over there!

gloomy.li: [write] Not that they'll read it properly.

plain.li: [greetings,warm] It lifted the whole house to hear from you, {WRITER}. Write again soon, and tell me how the harvest goes.
[greetings,warm,theirLowtech] Your words were read out at our fire, and the children asked for them twice. Come and sit with us when the roads are good.
[greetings,warm,theirHightech] Good to hear from you. We think well of your people here, and that is not said lightly in {TOWN}.
[greetings,warm,call] Always good to hear a friendly voice on this line. Call whenever you like, {WRITER}.
[greetings,cordial] Thank you for your letter. All is well in {TOWN}, and we wish the same for you.
[greetings,cordial,theirLowtech] The elders were glad of your words. May your fields be full and your nights quiet.
[greetings,cordial,call] Kind of you to call. Things are steady here, and we hope they are there too.
[greetings,cool] Your letter came. We are well enough, thank you.
[greetings,cool,call] Yes, we're well. Was there something else?
[greetings,curt] We have read your letter. There is nothing more to say for now.
[greetings,curt,war] We read your words. They change nothing between us.
[greetings,refusal] We do not care to keep up a correspondence. Do not trouble us again.
[greetings,refusal,war] Your people's hands are still red with ours. Keep your greetings.
[greetings,cordial,war] Strange, to get a kind word from your side. It will be remembered, for what it is worth.
[greetings,cool,war] We read it. Some here say it was kindly meant. Others are not so sure.
[condolences,warm] Your words about {TOPIC} reached us when we needed them most. You are a true friend to {TOWN}, {WRITER}.
[condolences,warm,theirLowtech] We held your letter at the burning and said your colony's name with the others who mourned. We will not forget it.
[condolences,warm,letter,theirLowtech] A letter written by hand, carried all that way, for our grief. The elders wept to hear it.
[condolences,cordial] Thank you for thinking of us. These have been hard days, and kind words help.
[condolences,cordial,call] It means something that you called. Thank you.
[condolences,cool] We thank you for your words. We grieve in our own way.
[condolences,cool,call] Thank you for calling. It is still raw here.
[condolences,curt] Your sympathy is noted.
[condolences,curt,war] Do not pretend to mourn with us.
[condolences,refusal] We have no wish to share our grief with your colony.
[condolences,cordial,war] Even enemies can mourn the same dead, it seems. We did not expect this from you.
[warning,warm] Your warning about {TOPIC} may have saved lives here. We have doubled the watch, and we owe you for it.
[warning,warm,theirLowtech] The scouts went out the night your words came. You did right by us, {WRITER}.
[warning,warm,call] Thank you for the word, we're moving people now. We won't forget this.
[warning,cordial] We had heard something of {TOPIC}, but not so much. Thank you for the warning.
[warning,cordial,call] Understood, and thank you. We'll keep our eyes open.
[warning,cool] We know of {TOPIC}. We can look after ourselves, but thank you.
[warning,curt] We are aware of the danger. We did not need you to tell us.
[warning,curt,war] Look to your own walls before you worry about ours.
[warning,refusal] We do not take warnings from strangers. Mind your own business.
[warning,cordial,war] Why your people would warn us, I do not know. But we listened.
[warning,cool,war] A warning from your side. We will see whether it is true.
[news,warm] You asked what we hear out here, so here is all of it. Come and trade when you can, we would be glad of you.
[news,warm,theirLowtech] The runners bring us everything the roads say, and we share it gladly with friends.
[news,cordial] Here is what we know, for what it is worth. Travel carefully.
[news,cordial,call] Let me see what we have heard lately. Here it is.
[news,cool] We can tell you a little.
[news,cool,war] We will tell you this much, and no more.
[news,curt] What we know is our own business. This much, then.
[news,refusal] We have nothing to tell your colony.
[news,refusal,war] Ask your own scouts.
[invitation,warm] Nothing would please me more. Set a place at your table, I will come as soon as the road allows.
[invitation,warm,theirLowtech] We will walk to you and sit at your fire. Tell your people to expect us.
[invitation,cordial] Thank you, I would be glad to see your colony for myself.
[invitation,cordial,call] I'd like that. I'll come out when I can.
[invitation,cool] A kind thought, but the season is a busy one. Perhaps another time.
[invitation,curt] I am needed here and cannot come.
[invitation,refusal] We do not visit your colony. You know why.
[help,warm] Of course. What we have is yours, and we send {HELP} gladly.
[help,warm,medicine] Our healers made up what we could spare. Use it well, and get well.
[help,warm,food] Nobody goes hungry while we have food to share. It is on its way.
[help,warm,theirLowtech] The elders said yes before I had finished reading. A friend asks, a friend gives.
[help,cordial] It is not much, but we can spare some {HELP}. Remember us when we are the ones who ask.
[help,cordial,call] We can manage a little. It goes out by courier, it won't come down the line.
[help,refusal] We are sorry, but we have nothing to spare this season.
[help,refusal] We cannot help you. Times are hard here too.
[help,refusal,theirLowtech] The elders talked it over and said no. We must keep what we have.
